# Capability Audit — ML Pipelines

**Source of truth:** the `ml/` Django app, federated across capability subdirectories (no single registry, unlike agents / spiders / PA tools). Each subdirectory under `ml/<capability>/` implements one ML approach (anomaly detection, GNN, RL, time series, training, etc.). AST-parsed; dataclass-shape classes (suffixes `Config`/`Prediction`/`Profile`/`Result`/`Stats`/`Sample` with short docstrings) are filtered out so the audit focuses on engine classes.

## Headline

- **Capability subdirectories:** 9
- **Primary engine/pipeline classes:** 24
- **Classes with docstrings:** 24 / 24
- **Top-level `ml/models.py`:** 1 Django model class(es).
- **Top-level `ml/tasks.py`:** 5 Celery task(s).

> ML is the most federated subsystem. Unlike `AGENT_MAP` or `PA_TOOL_SCHEMAS`, there's no single registry to introspect. Each capability lives in its own subdirectory; this audit walks them and pulls the primary engine class out of each.

## Findings

- `ml/tasks.py` defines 5 `@shared_task` functions. **`cleanup_old_model_files` is in the broken beat refs list** (see `docs/BEAT_AUDIT.md` finding 3 + `docs/AUDIT_FINDINGS.md` entry 3) — Celery autodiscover doesn't pick up `ml.tasks` at worker startup. Same fix as the others: add `'ml.tasks'` to `app.conf.imports` in `core/celery.py:317`.
